+    | ok _ _ _ hrl _ _ hsp hst =>
+      exact ((kstep_akeep (k := k) (.release hrl)).trans (kstep_akeep (.split hsp))).trans
+        (kstep_akeep (k := k) (.store hst))
+
+/-- `StackShape` is kept when the authorities are kept and each stack keeps its `internal` and
+its cells (DS-v1, non-normative; §42, §46). -/
+theorem stackShape_keep {D D' : DState} (hA : AKeep D.kern D'.kern) (hw : StackShape D)
+    (hs : ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), D'.stacks[i]? = some st' →
+      ∃ st : Stack, D.stacks[i]? = some st ∧ st'.internal = st.internal ∧ st'.cells = st.cells) :
+    StackShape D' := by
+  intro i st' h
+  obtain ⟨st, hst, hi, hc⟩ := hs i st' h
+  obtain ⟨y, hy, hm, hf⟩ := hw i st hst
+  obtain ⟨y', hy', hm', hf', -⟩ := hA _ y hy
+  exact ⟨y', hi ▸ hy', hm'.trans hm, fun c hc' => hf' ▸ hf c (hc ▸ hc')⟩
+
+/-- Replacing stack `j` by a stack with the same `internal` and cells (DS-v1, non-normative; §46
+metadata updates of `push`, `mark`, `rewind`, `grow`). -/
+theorem set_keeps {l : List Stack} {j : Nat} {st st₀ : Stack} (hst : l[j]? = some st₀)
+    (hi : st.internal = st₀.internal) (hc : st.cells = st₀.cells) :
+    ∀ (i : Nat) (st' : Stack), (l.set j st)[i]? = some st' →
+      ∃ st'' : Stack, l[i]? = some st'' ∧ st'.internal = st''.internal ∧
+        st'.cells = st''.cells := by
+  intro i st' h
+  rcases getElem?_set_cases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
+  · exact ⟨st₀, hst, hi, hc⟩
+  · exact ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩
+
+/-- Every library step keeps `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §76.2, §76.3 at `newStack`,
+§42 afterwards). -/
+theorem DStep.stackShape {k : K} {D D' : DState} (h : DStep k D D') (hw : StackShape D) :
+    StackShape D' := by
+  have hA := h.akeep
+  cases h with
+  | kernel => exact stackShape_keep hA hw fun i st' h => ⟨st', h, rfl, rfl⟩
+  | @newStack _ _ _ int hs =>
+    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hs
+    intro i st' h
+    rcases getElem?_append_single h with h | rfl
+    · exact hw i st' h
+    · have hi := hp.base.internalAuth
+      cases hy : D.kern.A[int]? with
+      | none => rw [hy] at hi; exact hi.elim
+      | some y =>
+        rw [hy] at hi
+        refine ⟨y, hy, hi.2, fun c hc => ?_⟩
+        have := hp.base.fpSup c hc; simpa [S3.afp, hy] using this
+  | push hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
+  | mark hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
+  | rewind hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
+  | grow hs => cases hs with | ok hst => exact stackShape_keep hA hw (set_keeps hst rfl rfl)
+
+/-- Every library-reachable state satisfies `StackShape` (DS-v1, non-normative; §47: no stack
+initially; §76.2, §76.3, §42). -/
+theorem DReach.stackShape {k : K} {statics : Statics} {D : DState} (h : DReach k statics D) :
+    StackShape D := by
+  induction h with
+  | init => intro i st h; simp [DState.init] at h
+  | step _ hs ih => exact hs.stackShape ih
+
+/-- The authority added by `split` of `src` on one region can be released at once (support for
+DS-v1, non-normative, `rewind`; §62): it is active, derived, held by the current frame (§62.1,
+§62.2), has no descendant (§62.3: origins precede, §42) and, under `DBound`, anchors no place
+(§62.3, §62.4). -/
+theorem release_after_split {s : S3} {src : Nat} {R : List Nat} (hb : DBound s) :
+    ReleasePre (splitEff s src [R]) s.A.length := by
+  have hy₀ := split_block s src R
+  refine ⟨⟨_, hy₀, rfl⟩, by rw [hy₀]; simp [OptP], by rw [hy₀]; exact rfl,
+    fun j hj hn => ?_, fun q _ _ hx => absurd (hb q _ hx) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩
+  have := chain_lt hn
+  have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [splitEff] at this; omega
+
+/-- `rewind_ok_iff` (DS-v1, non-normative: "rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an
+active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to
+available"; §36; §61.1, §61.3, §62 through Part XIV). On a library-reachable state (`DReach`, a
+state invariant), for an existing stack, `rewind m` is `ok` exactly when `m` is a live mark of the
+stack (DS-v1), the administrative right of §36 holds (`AdminRight`), and no active authority
+derived from `internal` covers a cell above `m` (DS-v1). The model has no explicit check of the
+last condition: it is the effective `Modify` of `internal` required by `split` (§61.1, with the
+effective mode of §43). The other checks of `split` and `release` never reject there: `internal`
+has own mode `Modify` and covers the cells (`DReach.stackShape`, §76.2, §76.3), and anchors name
+existing authorities (`dBound_of_reachable`). DS-v1 does not list §36: a reachable state where
+only §36 rejects is `Witness.reading_rewind_right`. -/

+    {j : Nat} {st : Stack} (hst : D.stacks[j]? = some st) {m : Mark} :
+    (∃ D', RewindStep k j m D (.ok D')) ↔

+        ∀ (x l : Nat) (y : Authority), D.kern.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
+          st.internal ∈ D.kern.ancs x → l ∈ y.footprint → l ∉ above st m := by

+    have hab : ∀ l ∈ above st m, l ∈ yi.footprint :=
+      fun l hl => hci l (List.mem_of_mem_drop (List.mem_of_mem_take hl))
+    have hmod : ∀ l ∈ above st m, effective D.kern st.internal l = some .modify := by
+      intro l hl
+      have hd : descModes D.kern st.internal l = [] := by
+        apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
+        obtain ⟨x, y, hy, ya, hly, hx, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
+        exact hno x l y hy ya hx hly hl
+      rw [effective_eq hyi yia (hab l hl), hd]; simp [effOf, hmi]
+    have hex : D.kern.ExercisableAt st.internal .modify := by
+      have hmr := ha.2
+      simp only [MetaRight, arenaValue, Stack.entry, hyi] at hmr
+      cases hv : yi.holder with

+      | place v =>

+      refine ⟨ha.1, hex, fun r hr p hp => ?_, fun r hr p hp => ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _,

+      · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr] at hp
+        exact ⟨by simp only [S3.afp, hyi]; exact hab p hp, by rw [hmod p hp]; simp⟩

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.
----

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

626:**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.
904:4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
910:The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.
916:1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.

DS-v1 has no notion of stack death. The spec's nearest analogue treats a dead administration as a static check, i.e. reject: §77.1, "The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active".

At most, this would be a new, separate note on DS-R3, not a defect in the B47 records.
